scope: Stateless browser-context disposal, bounded HTTP responses, and admission ownership. This is not a WAF access or hosted-parity result.

observedProblem.fullRunReceipt: Previous source2476425 full100 run had158 Page-close confirmations and157 context-close acknowledgements; one Target context acknowledgement was unconfirmed.
observedProblem.causalLimit: That receipt alone cannot distinguish an open context from a lost/late acknowledgement. Owned fault injection establishes the implementation defects; it does not retrospectively prove the public Target cause.
ownedReproduction: A real close event with a lost acknowledgement was reported as an unfinished context.
Terminal cleanup and outer finally could issue duplicate close commands.
After a timed-out context allocation, a second request could allocate before the first request had finished allocating and disposing.

implementation: Observe the close event immediately when the stateless context is allocated, before route setup.
Share one disposal command and close-event promise across terminal capture cleanup and outer finally.
A fulfilled, rejected, or timed-out close command alone cannot establish context disposal.
Retain admission through unfinished context allocation or disposal while returning the bounded HTTP response.
Release admission when actual context closure is confirmed, including closure after a timed-out request.

cases: Actual context close with a lost acknowledgement reports closed and issues one command.
A held close retains admission beyond both HTTP cleanup wait bounds, prevents a second context, and recovers after disposal.
A held allocation times out, prevents a second allocation, disposes the late context, and recovers.
limits: Owned injected faults are not measurements of commercial WAF behavior.
Before and after fault-test durations are not a matched production latency benchmark; failing assertions short-circuit the before cases.
Retained session disposal is outside this change. A context that never closes continues to occupy admission until owner shutdown.
